newsitem.title: GERMANY: TENNIS-MANAGER SILENT ON REPORT BECKER TO LEAVE GERMANY.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-MANAGER SILENT ON REPORT BECKER TO LEAVE GERMANY.

text.p: Boris Becker's manager on Friday declined to comment on a newspaper report the tennis star was so upset about an investigation into his tax affairs that he planned to leave Germany next week for good.

Germany's Bild daily, quoting close friends of the tennis star, said a trip to Florida next week to prepare for a tournament in Key Biscayne would be Becker's final farewell to Germany and his Munich home.
"I'm not making any comment. I'm not denying or passing any judgment on anything," manager Axel Meyer-Woelden said when asked about the report.
Bild ran the front page story beside a picture of Becker and his wife Barbara with their backs to the camera under the headline "Boris gone forever!".
"He's finished with Germany," the paper quoted a "very close confidant" of Becker as saying. "He's really already left, ever since the tax investigators raided his house."
Officials searched the former Wimbledon champion's home in December as part of an inquiry into his finances. They have declined to comment on the details of the probe and no charges have been filed.
Many German sports figures live abroad to avoid the relatively high rates of tax in their homeland.

The father of Steffi Graf, one of the the few stars who stayed, was convicted last month of avoiding more than 12 million marks in tax on her income. Peter Graf, who managed his daughter's financial affairs, was sentenced to almost four years in jail but remains free pending an appeal.
Bild said Becker has spent only five days in Munich since the tax raid, although he has played little tennis because of injury.

Bild said Becker had told his friend: "The tax hunters have taken away my home. My house was like a protective fortress, the last remainder of my private life. Only friends and family were here. Now everything's strange."
Becker, ranked number 12 in the world, has previously said he planned to leave Germany when his son Noah, aged three, starts attending school in about three years time.
The tennis star thinks his son would have a better chance of leading a normal life outside Germany.

But Friday's story was the first report of any plans for an imminent departure. Becker spent much of career based in Monte Carlo but returned to Germany just three years ago -- to the delight of his home fans.
Bild said Becker felt angry at the Munich authorities, who had even searched private diaries and his son's room, and was considering taking action against them for betraying confidential information.

"Boris lived out his tennis bag for 10 years. He looked for and found a permanent place in Munich. His tax advisers were against a return to Germany from Monte Carlo. But Boris really wanted to. And now this!" a "close friend" told the paper.
